blocks.path: Cataracts in adults
s: Cataracts is where the lens in your eye becomes cloudy, causing blurred vision and loss of sight.
It usually affects older adults and can be treated with surgery.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults
s: This page is about cataracts in adults.
Find out about cataracts in children.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: Symptoms of cataracts usually develop slowly.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: You'll often have cataracts in both eyes but the symptoms may be different in each eye.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: Symptoms include:

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: blurred vision

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: difficulty seeing at night

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: difficulty reading and watching television

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: your eyes being uncomfortable in, or sensitive to, light and glare

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: looking at 1 object but seeing 2 (double vision)

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: seeing glowing rings (halos) around lights

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: colours look faded, especially blue

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Symptoms of cataracts in adults
s: If you wear glasses, you may notice that you need to change the prescription of your glasses more often than usual.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Non-urgent advice: See an optician if:
s: you have symptoms of cataracts

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Non-urgent advice: See an optician if:
s: If they think you have cataracts, they'll refer you to an eye specialist for more tests or treatment.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: You may be more likely to get cataracts if:

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: you're aged 60 or over

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: you've had an eye injury or eye surgery in the past

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: you have another eye condition, such as uveitis or being very short-sighted

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: you've taken steroid medicines for long periods of time

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: you smoke

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: a parent, brother or sister has had cataracts

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: you're a woman

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: your eyes have been regularly exposed to a lot of sunlight without protection such as sunglasses

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Causes of cataracts in adults
s: Some long-term health conditions can also increase your risk of getting cataracts, such as type 2 diabetes, severe dermatitis and high blood pressure.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: Cataracts do not usually need treatment straight away.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: Over time cataracts will get worse and you'll need cataract surgery if you want to to improve your sight.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: A GP or eye specialist will talk to you about whether or not you want surgery.
This may depend on:

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: how cataracts are affecting your daily life

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: if cataracts are in one or both eyes

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: If you decide to have surgery, there may be a wait for treatment.
Ask your eye specialist how long you'll have to wait.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: Cataract surgery is done under a local anaesthetic.
This means you'll be awake but you will not feel any pain.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: The cloudy lens is replaced with an artificial one.
You should be able to go home on the same day.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery)
s: If you have cataracts in both eyes, they'll be treated on separate days.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > Treatment for cataracts (cataract surgery) > Find out more:
s: Cataract surgery

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > How cataracts affect your life
s: Cataracts affect your sight and without treatment will eventually cause sight loss.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > How cataracts affect your life
s: Using stronger glasses and brighter light for reading may help for a while.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > How cataracts affect your life
s: For most people, cataract surgery will help to improve their vision.
Recovery from surgery is quick and serious complications are rare.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > How cataracts affect your life > Driving with cataracts
s: You may still be able to drive if your vision is good enough.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > How cataracts affect your life > Driving with cataracts
s: You must let the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) know if your eyesight does not meet the minimum standards needed for driving.

blocks.path: Cataracts in adults > How cataracts affect your life > Driving with cataracts
s: Ask an optician if you are not sure.
